analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-17. Event date: Not reported in the supplied evidence. investigation occurred on or before publication date.
analysis.location_and_population: United States, California, San Quentin Rehabilitation Center (a prison housing low- and medium-security inmates, capacity >3,000).
analysis.event: A suspected hantavirus case in an inmate at San Quentin Rehabilitation Center was investigated and later determined to be a false positive following confirmatory PCR testing. The investigation was coordinated by the California Department of Public Health (CDPH), California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation (CDCR), and Marin County Public Health.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: No confirmed hantavirus cases, deaths, or exposures reported. Facility decontamination and monitoring of prisoners and staff were conducted as precautionary measures. Hantavirus is rare in the U.S. (890 laboratory-confirmed cases since 1993), with no vaccine or specific antiviral treatment available.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Initial antibody test returned positive but was later ruled a false positive via PCR testing at CDPH’s Viral and Rickettsial Diseases Laboratory. Authorities decontaminated inmate housing and are monitoring individuals. No further details on clinical information or additional testing provided. The San Quentin Rehabilitation Center did not respond to inquiries.

analysis.brief_en: California health officials confirmed a suspected hantavirus case at San Quentin Rehabilitation Center was a false positive after confirmatory PCR testing. The investigation, led by the California Department of Public Health, involved antibody testing followed by more specific PCR analysis, which returned negative. Authorities decontaminated inmate housing and are monitoring prisoners and staff as a precaution. Hantavirus remains rare in the U.S., with 890 confirmed cases since 1993 and no available vaccine or specific antiviral treatment.

title: Colorado adult dies from hantavirus after local rodent exposure - AOL.com

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-17. Event date: Not reported in the supplied evidence. Time range: Spring or summer 2026 (implied by seasonal context).
analysis.location_and_population: Douglas County, Colorado, United States. Affected population: One adult resident. Hosts: Wild rodents (deer mice, white-footed mice).
analysis.event: A confirmed hantavirus infection in an adult resident of Douglas County, Colorado, resulting in death. Reported by the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment and local news outlets. The infection is not linked to a recent cruise ship outbreak.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Scale: Rare disease with 1–2 dozen U.S. cases annually (e.g., 26 cases in 2023). cases (1993–2023): 890, including 121 in Colorado. Risk to general public remains low. Sin Nombre hantavirus does not spread person-to-person.

analysis.brief_en: A Colorado adult has died from hantavirus infection, confirmed by state health officials and local media. The case, reported in Douglas County, is not connected to a recent cruise ship outbreak. Hantavirus, primarily carried by wild rodents such as deer mice, is transmitted via inhalation of contaminated particles. The disease is rare in the U.S., with 1–2 dozen cases annually, though Colorado has recorded 121 cases since 1993. Health authorities emphasize the risk to the general public remains low, as person-to-person transmission does not occur with the Sin Nombre strain.

title: Al Roker Reveals Daughter Is Married, Says CDC Asked Him to Test for Hantavirus on Return Trip - AOL.com

analysis.time: Published on 2026-07-16. Event dates: April 2026 (initial cases and deaths on MV Hondius cruise ship), May 9, 2026 (ship docked in Tenerife), May 12, 2026 (Al Roker's Today show remarks).
analysis.location_and_population: Global (passengers from at least 12 countries), with specific locations: MV Hondius cruise ship (originating from Argentina), Tenerife (Canary Islands, Spain), Omaha, Nebraska (USA). Affected populations: cruise ship passengers (150 total), including Dutch, German, and American nationals.
analysis.event: A hantavirus outbreak occurred aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship, reported by media and discussed by Al Roker on the Today show. The event is confirmed with nine cases and three deaths. The CDC requested voluntary testing from travelers returning from Europe, though the specific pathogen was not disclosed.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Scale: 9 confirmed hantavirus cases, 3 deaths (Dutch man, German woman, and Dutch woman). Impact: Ship diverted to Tenerife for evacuation. 30 passengers disembarked early in St. remaining passengers quarantined. Risk: WHO assessed the risk of a worldwide outbreak as currently low.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Investigation: WHO theorized a Dutch couple may have contracted the virus during a pre-cruise trip in Chile/Argentina. Testing: CDC requested voluntary testing from travelers. one American tested 'mildly' positive for the Andes strain, another had mild symptoms. Isolation: Passengers quarantined in Tenerife and Omaha. Uncertainty: Transmission route on the ship remains unspecified. CDC did not confirm the pathogen for which testing was requested.

analysis.brief_en: A hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship resulted in nine confirmed cases and three deaths (Dutch, German, and Dutch nationals) since April 2026. The ship, carrying 150 passengers from at least 12 countries, docked in Tenerife on May 9 after 30 passengers disembarked early. Remaining passengers were quarantined, with 18 Americans flown to Omaha, Nebraska. The CDC requested voluntary testing from travelers returning from Europe, though the specific pathogen was not disclosed. The WHO assessed the risk of a worldwide outbreak as low.
